_note: Claims register — every load-bearing figure this site publishes, the source that carries it, and the exact string that must be present in that source. Checked daily by scripts/check-claims.py against the LIVE site and the LIVE sources, so it verifies what is published rather than what is in the tree. Not a changelog and not a style guide: an entry earns its place only if the site states something a reader could check. Written 2026-08-26 after a figure sat live for 14 days beside a citation that never contained it. Re-pinned 2026-09-16 after the 2026-09-15 rewrite left eight entries pointing at copy that no longer existed; the canonical product sentence is now pinned here too, against the server README that owns it (see EDITORIAL.md).

contract.role: Authority for what may be claimed about EISV and in what words.

stop-rule.role: Defines the single pre-registered outcome read and its kill criterion.

agents-readme.role: States which parts of agents/ are the public contract and which are examples.

readme.role: The server's own front page. Authority for the one-sentence definition, the install path, and the loop.

evidence-limits.role: The current evidence ledger. Authority for mechanism, outcome, benefit scope, the tool catalog, and the deployment start date.

resident-readme.role: The resident project's own status and product-boundary statement.

mcp-clients.role: Authority for the client-facing endpoint and the client-neutrality claim.

testbed-prereg.role: The frozen evaluation plan for the federated multi-principal testbed. Authority for what that benchmark measures and for whether it has been run.

claims.site_says: federation kernel connects independent runtimes to one operator-controlled server over MCP or HTTP
must_contain: UNITARES is self-hosted accountability infrastructure for operators running
Its federation kernel connects independent runtimes to one operator-controlled server over MCP or HTTP
Agent work should remain attributable, reviewable, and recoverable even when the process that started it is gone
claims.why: The one-sentence definition is owned by the server README and copied here verbatim. Ten different phrasings were live across the site, the repository, and the share cards on 2026-09-16; this pin is what keeps it at one.

must_contain: git clone --branch "v$v" --depth 1 https://github.com/cirwel/unitares.git && cd unitares && docker compose up -d --wait
claims.why: The site prints the README's command, not one of its own. An install command that differs from the server's is the first thing an integrator notices and the last thing anyone re-checks.
The deployment start date is engraved on the seal and stated in the receipts. If the evidence ledger ever re-dates the first identity record, the seal is wrong the same day.

claims.site_says: The complete tool catalog is callable on every transport
must_contain: one complete catalog remains negotiable and callable on every transport
the default initial listing is progressive and omitted names run through `use_tool` after discovery
claims.why: The initial listing is progressive after unitares #2328. Every capability remains discoverable and callable; the site must not promise every schema in the initial listing.

must_contain: git clone --branch "v$v" --depth 1 https://github.com/cirwel/unitares.git && cd unitares && docker compose up -d --wait
claims.why: Same command as the home page, checked separately because it is stated on a second page.

claims.site_says: Zero of seven streams beat last-value persistence
must_contain: The per-agent reference does useful work
0/7 streams beat persistence
win rates 0.32–0.48
Three of the seven nominal
claims.why: The page states all three caveats the contract attaches, including the one about three of seven agents being the same Pi. If the contract ever drops a caveat, the page is carrying a claim its source no longer supports.

claims.site_says: this reconstruction did not earn its description
must_contain: BENCHMARK FAIL for the cold-start reconstruction; UNIDENTIFIED for the warmed deployed EMA
claims.why: The page must not upgrade a reconstruction's benchmark failure into a verdict on the reference that actually runs.

claims.site_says: Unresolved is not the same as negative
must_contain: WITHDRAWN FOR TARGET INFERENCE
the question is unresolved, not negative
claims.why: The page files this question under open rather than closed. If the contract re-closes it in either direction, the page's own section structure is wrong, not just its wording.

must_contain: WITHDRAWN FOR TARGET INFERENCE
claims.why: The withdrawal is the reason the question is open. If the contract ever un-withdraws the read, the sentence is stating a status that no longer holds.

claims.site_says: scheduled for December 2026 with a kill criterion
must_contain: kill criterion
claims.why: Both the date and the existence of a written kill criterion are load-bearing; 'pre-registered' without one is just a plan.

claims.site_says: No benchmark run has been executed
must_contain: No headline, ablation, or scale-sweep runs had been
claims.why: The page files Question II as designed and frozen but not run. Every drift here runs in the direction that flatters the page, so if the registration ever records completed headline runs the status line must change with it.

claims.site_says: prompt-only, log-only, federated per-principal runtime governance, and a centralized-governor reference
must_contain: prompt-only, log-only, federated per-principal
centralized-governor reference
claims.why: The four regimes are the whole measurement claim: without the centralized-governor arm the price of decentralization would be asserted rather than measured. Naming them on the page requires the frozen registration to still name them.

claims.site_says: built on it and are explicitly not part of it
must_contain: not** part of the public contract
examples of how to build a resident agent, not as load-bearing governance internals
claims.why: The whole four-tier claim rests on the reference workloads being examples rather than contract. If that line ever softens, the page is describing a boundary the repo no longer draws.

must_contain: http://localhost:8767/mcp/
Any client that supports Streamable HTTP MCP
claims.why: This page hands a reader a port and a path to paste into a config file. A wrong one costs them an afternoon, and the client-neutrality sentence is what licenses printing the config without naming a vendor.

claims.site_says: No governed-versus-ungoverned comparison has yet shown an incident prevented or an outcome improved
must_contain: No governed-versus-ungoverned comparison has shown an incident prevented or an outcome improved by pausing
Incident prevention or benefit from pausing
claims.why: The one guard that matters on a page written to get people to install something. A build page is where an unearned benefit claim would be most useful and least honest, so the disclaimer is pinned to the server's own words rather than to this page's restraint.

claims.site_says: with no change to the server's repository at all
must_contain: unitares.resident_progress_sources
no change to this repo is required
claims.why: The strongest plug-and-play claim on the site and the only one that says an adopter never has to touch the server repository. It is quoted from agents/README.md and must not outlive it.

claims.site_says: early skeleton, not yet a usable general-purpose agent
must_contain: early skeleton
not a usable general-purpose agent
claims.why: An UNDERclaim, pinned for the same reason as the overclaims. If unitares-resident matures and the README drops this line, the build page will be talking a reader out of the very thing it should be pointing them at.

claims.site_says: UNITARES is the record behind them, not the transport between them
must_contain: UNITARES is the record behind them, not the transport between them
claims.why: A boundary, and the kind that decays quietly: it disclaims cross-runtime interoperability, which A2A owns. The 2026-09 claims audit graded 'federation' unsupported as read for exactly this reason. If the README ever drops the disclaimer, the site must stop implying it too, so the two move together or the check goes red.

retired_phrasings.why: Labelled the maintainer's own development environment as production. It is where the system is used every day, not a production deployment for anyone else.
